analysis: Reviewed three changed files. (1) LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift adds a test (head lines 181-203) asserting that EngineV2Factory.prefillChunkKey and stepTokenBudgetKey pass through LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment into the launchd plist. UNRELATED_SECRET stays excluded, and the watchdog passthrough does not carry the keys. This is test-only and confirms the allowlist remains narrow. The production allowlist change itself is not in this batch, so I could not review it; the keys are non-secret performance tuning values. (2) scripts/gemma_contbatch/config.py only adds comments (lines 33-37) and leaves SCHEMA_VERSION at 6. (3) scripts/gemma_contbatch/validation.py (line 16) adds scheduler prefill schema version 5 to the accepted raw schema tuple. It is a benchmark script outside the runtime trust boundaries. It only widens the accepted schema set to a version the PR describes as reviewed, and the existing finite, model-ID and matrix checks still apply. The change touches no coordinator-provider WebSocket contract, attestation, App Attest authorization, key handling, prefix-cache storage (T-041) or other threat-model assets. Remaining question for integration: the production changes behind the new prefill chunk and step-budget env keys and the larger Gemma chunking (2048 chunk, 4096 step) were not supplied. Whether they affect resource limits or DoS exposure (T-010, T-029) and the prefix-cache adoption behavior (T-041) cannot be assessed from this batch.
